stem.text: The function g is defined on the closed interval \( [-2, 3] \) and is twice differentiable at every x in that interval except \( x = 2 \), where g has a jump discontinuity. Also \( g'(0) = 0 \) and \( g''(0) > 0 \). Must g attain an absolute minimum value on the closed interval \( [-2, 3] \)? Justify the answer.

answer_key.label: No, because g is not continuous on the closed interval \( [-2, 3] \), so the Extreme Value Theorem does not apply.

worked_solution.text: g has a jump discontinuity at \( x = 2 \), inside the interval, so g is not continuous on \( [-2, 3] \).
A hypothesis of the Extreme Value Theorem fails, so the theorem gives no conclusion and g need not attain an absolute minimum value.

options.label: Yes, because g has a relative minimum at \( x = 0 \), so its absolute minimum value is \( g(0) \).
options.derivation: the relative extremum found by the second derivative test reported as the absolute one
